p0-w5.question: Between which potentials vs Li+/Li are CaCO3 and the native Al oxide at equilibrium against lithiation (Li-open grand potential) and against oxidation that releases CO2 and O2 with the cation taken up by the anion of each registered electrolyte salt? Does the registered regime range [E_cell_min, E_cell_max] lie inside each window under every gas-reference scheme? (thermodynamic windows; no kinetic statement)
p0-w5.scope: Thermodynamic proxies only: a stability domain, a decomposition energy or a window says which state is at equilibrium, never how fast anything corrodes, dissolves or decomposes.

R-cell.convention: theory contract E_window = Delta_G_r/(Delta_n_Li F_c); E_ox = min over Delta_n_Li > 0

sink_assumption.statement: The solvated sink needs the free energy of Ca2+ and Al3+ relative to Li+ in the electrolyte solvent; both keys are gaps at this params sha, so it is undetermined.

notes: reduction does not depend on the gas scheme (no gas in lithiation)
oxidation: lowest over the schemes; the cp2 rule F5 verdict is in extensions.p0-w5
